mcqs.question: What is the correct definition of average power?

options.A: Average power is the total work done divided by the total time taken, P_{avg}=W/\Delta t.
options.B: Average power is the maximum work done per unit time.
options.C: Average power is the energy stored in a system.
options.D: Average power is the force applied divided by distance.

mcqs.answer: Average power is the total work done divided by the total time taken, P_{avg}=W/\Delta t.
mcqs.explanation: Average power is defined as the work done divided by the time interval during which the work is done, P_{avg}=W/\Delta t. Option B describes a maximum, not an average. Option C confuses power with stored energy. Option D mixes force and distance, which gives work, not power.

mcqs.question: A particle experiences an instantaneous force \(F\) and moves with instantaneous velocity \(v\). Which expression gives the instantaneous power delivered to the particle?
mcqs.explanation: Instantaneous power is the time derivative of work: dW/dt. Since dW = F·dx, dividing by dt gives dW/dt = F·dx/dt = F·v. Hence P = Fv. The other options are not dimensionally consistent with power.

mcqs.question: A motor does 500 J of work in 10 s. What is its average power?
mcqs.explanation: Average power P = work/time = 500 J / 10 s = 50 W. Option A is ten times smaller, C is hundred times larger, and D is far too small.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to force and velocity
mcqs.question: A car engine exerts a constant force of 2000 N on the car while the car moves at a constant speed of 15 m/s. What is the mechanical power delivered by the engine?
mcqs.explanation: Power P = F·v = 2000 N × 15 m/s = 30,000 W (or 30 kW). Options B, C, D are obtained by dividing the correct value by factors of 10, 100, and 150 respectively, which are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines average power?

options.A: Average power equals the work done divided by the time taken.
options.B: Average power equals the force multiplied by the distance traveled.
options.C: Average power equals the energy per unit mass.
options.D: Average power equals the velocity divided by the force.

mcqs.answer: Average power equals the work done divided by the time taken.
mcqs.explanation: The definition of average power is work per unit time (P = W/Δt). Option B describes work (force × distance), not power. Option C describes specific energy, and option D has incorrect dimensions.

mcqs.question: Why is instantaneous power given by the product of instantaneous force and instantaneous velocity?

options.A: Because power is the rate of change of momentum, which equals force times velocity.
options.B: Because power is the time derivative of work, and dW = F·dx, so dW/dt = F·dx/dt = F·v.
options.C: Because power is the product of mass and acceleration.
options.D: Because power is independent of velocity.

mcqs.answer: Because power is the time derivative of work, and dW = F·dx, so dW/dt = F·dx/dt = F·v.
mcqs.explanation: Work done in an infinitesimal displacement is dW = F·dx. Dividing by dt gives instantaneous power: P = dW/dt = F·dx/dt = F·v. Option A confuses momentum with work. Option C describes force (F = m·a), not power. Option D is false because power depends on velocity when force is present.

mcqs.question: Machine A does 2000 J of work in 5 s, while Machine B does 3000 J of work in 10 s. Which machine has the greater average power and what is its value?

options.C: Both have the same power, 400 W
options.D: Both have the same power, 300 W

mcqs.explanation: Power of A = 2000 J / 5 s = 400 W. Power of B = 3000 J / 10 s = 300 W. Therefore Machine A has the higher average power of 400 W. Options B, C, and D give incorrect comparisons or values.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to force and velocity
mcqs.question: A particle moves under a force that is directly proportional to its instantaneous velocity: \(F = k\,v\), where \(k\) is a constant. What is the expression for the instantaneous power of the particle in terms of \(k\) and \(v\)?
mcqs.explanation: Instantaneous power P = F·v. Substituting F = k v gives P = (k v)·v = k v^{2}. Option B omits one factor of v, C inverts the relationship, and D would imply power is constant, which is incorrect.
